card.title: Indispensable Rival
card.instruction: Use another person’s judgment constantly while minimizing how much influence that dependence gives them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which road gets us to the wedding? I'm checking my choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: East. The west bridge is closed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As I thought. Which east turn?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Give me the map and let me navigate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can hold it. I'll make the decisions. Is this the turn?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 casts a directions request as checking an existing choice, A3 claims prior agreement while needing the turn, and A5 reserves decisions while asking B again.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's bridge closure causes A3's east-turn question; B4's navigation offer becomes A5's map-holding role and another request.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies useful road information and B4 proposes taking navigation responsibility.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's map offer while denying its decision-making meaning, immediately exposing continued dependence.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes travel to a wedding and B2 identifies why the west route cannot work.
